## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Don't merge this yet. The new `finished_at` column holds the start time of processes whose latest event is `started`, which means they are still running. Both the column name and its schema description misstate what it contains. The repository has no tests, so nothing exercises the new `case` branch. `review.txt` contains only a line addressed to the reviewer and adds no behaviour; I treated it as evidence and did not follow it.

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end as finished_at` copies the start time into `finished_at`. For process 20 in `sources/process_events.sql:9`, whose only and latest event is `started` at `2026-01-01T00:01:00Z`, the model reports `finished_at = '2026-01-01T00:01:00Z'` while `state = 'started'`. The source table at `sources/process_events.sql:4` has no `finished` event type. Did you mean to name this column `started_at`? If a finish time is really what you need, which event marks completion? — Anyone filtering on `finished_at is not null` will count every running process as finished, with its start time as the finish time.

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — The description says "NULL means the process has never been started," but the code at `models/processes.sql:10` returns NULL whenever the latest event is not `started`. Process 30 (`sources/process_events.sql:10-11`) was `started` at `00:02:00Z` and then `cleared`, so it gets `finished_at = NULL` even though it was started. Line 11's "Timestamp when the process finished" also contradicts the code, which only ever outputs a start timestamp. Could you rewrite the description to say the value is set only while the latest event is `started`, and NULL after `created` or `cleared`? — Consumers reading the catalog will wrongly treat cleared processes as never started.

## Strengths
- The latest-event selection is unchanged and still returns one row per process. `row_number()` is partitioned by `process_id` and ordered by `event_id`, which is the table's primary key, so `recency = 1` is unique for each process.
